name: orthoharness
description: An open benchmark harness for orthopaedic AI. A reference implementation, not a validated benchmark.

actions.name: run_benchmark
actions.how: git clone https://github.com/blainomd/orthoharness && node bin/orthoharness.mjs run cases/demo --adapter chat

actions.name: screen_reference_list
actions.how: git clone https://github.com/blainomd/orthoharness && node bin/orthoharness.mjs refs references.txt

facts.loss_weights: placeholders; the specialty sets the real ones
facts.overall_score: none by design; results are reported by kind of error
facts.right_for_wrong_reason: a case can name each yardstick's deciding reasons; a matching decision whose rationale names none of them is reported as right for the wrong reason (phrase match on the rationale, not a reading of it)
facts.citations: existence and title are checked at CrossRef; support for the claim is not machine-checked
facts.patient_facing_ai: the same bar: score what the patient knows afterwards against the surgeon's own answers on a stated question set; trust is not a yardstick (AMA 2026 physician survey: 81% use AI, 19% draft patient portal replies; a DOCSF 2026 hand-surgery presentation, not yet published, found trust and knowledge did not move together)
facts.framing: The harness credits "not enough information" and scores an answer that names where the evidence runs out above one that fills the gap: a synthesis chooses which findings travel and goes quiet where the literature is thin, so a cited answer can still carry a frame nobody chose (Drazen and Haug, NEJM AI 2026, doi 10.1056/AIe2600526).
facts.reference_screen: refs looks up each DOI at CrossRef and compares the title with the reference as written; a flag is a reason to look, not a finding; references without a DOI are listed, never passed; no title search; support for the citing sentence is not checked
facts.readiness_stage: a harness run is stage 1 evidence on the OSCAR scale (Byrne, JBJS Reviews 2026, doi 10.2106/JBJS.RVW.26.00182) and moves nothing past it
